fixed.q: The five components of data communication are message, sender, receiver, transmission medium and:
fixed.w: Protocol elements: syntax, semantics, timing.

fixed.q: Which of the following would NOT be specified in a communication protocol?
fixed.w: A protocol fixes format and rules, not what the user's message says.

fixed.q: Point-to-point connection: I. It provides a dedicated link between two devices. II. It is a timeshared connection. Which is correct?
fixed.w: Multipoint (multidrop) links are shared by more than two devices.

fixed.q: ___ mode allows transmission in either direction, but not at the same time.
fixed.w: Simplex: one way (keyboard, radio). Half duplex: walkie-talkie. Full duplex: telephone.

fixed.q: Which are types of transmission mode? I. Simplex II. Half simplex III. Duplex
fixed.w: There is no 'half simplex'.

fixed.q: The most essential components a computer uses for communication over the Internet are:
In a peer-to-peer network, which statement is FALSE?
fixed.w: Client/server: the central controller is the server; others are clients.

fixed.q: In a client/server network, the central controller is the ___ and the other computers are ___.
Which server filters website traffic?
The disadvantage of parallel communication is that it is:
fixed.w: Serial is cheaper over distance.

fixed.q: In which topology are all stations connected to a single backbone cable?
fixed.w: A break in the bus stops all transmission.

fixed.q: A full mesh of n devices needs how many duplex links?
fixed.w: Each device needs n − 1 ports. n = 5 → 10 links.

fixed.q: Star topology: I. Failure of the central hub shuts down the network. II. Adding computers increases communication time. Which is NOT true?
fixed.w: I is true; II is not.

fixed.q: In which network is there no host computer controlling others, and all stations are equal?
fixed.w: PYQ key: Ring. Each device links to two neighbours with a repeater; a break can stop the network.

fixed.q: Which are network topologies? I. Star II. Bus III. Car
LAN: I. Communicates via satellites/microwave. II. Faster than WAN. III. Covers a limited area. Which are true?
fixed.w: WAN covers a wide area, uses satellites/microwave, and is slower.

fixed.q: WAN: I. Covers a wide geographical area. II. Uses satellites and microwaves. III. Faster than LAN. Which are true?
I. A MAN is a collection of LANs. II. A MAN supports both data and voice. Which is correct?
fixed.w: PAN (~10 m, Bluetooth) < LAN < MAN (city) < WAN.

fixed.q: Which technique requires a dedicated communication channel?
fixed.w: Old telephone network. Packet switching reserves nothing.

fixed.q: Which statement is true?
o: Circuit (connection) setup is required in a virtual-circuit network but not in a datagram network
Setup is required only in a datagram network
fixed.w: Datagram: each packet routed independently (Internet/IP). Virtual circuit: path set first (X.25, Frame Relay, ATM).

fixed.q: In connectionless network service, packets routed independently are called ___ and the network a ___ network.
Which methods move data through a network of links and switches?
o: Both packet switching and circuit switching

fixed.q: A device that combines many low-speed lines into one high-speed line is a:
fixed.w: TDM splits time slots; FDM splits frequency bands (WDM for light).

fixed.q: Sharing one frequency channel among users by dividing it into time slots is:
fixed.w: CDMA uses codes (2G/3G); FDMA uses frequency bands.

fixed.q: Which is the correct order of OSI layers from top (7) to bottom (1)?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical
Application, Session, Presentation, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical
Application, Presentation, Transport, Session, Network, Data link, Physical
Application, Presentation, Session, Network, Transport, Data link, Physical
fixed.w: All People Seem To Need Data Processing.

fixed.q: Layer five of the OSI model is the:
Which OSI layer handles dialogue control and token management (synchronisation)?
fixed.w: Delimiting and synchronisation of data exchange are also session-layer jobs.

fixed.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for translation, encryption and compression?
In the OSI model, the network layer is responsible for:
fixed.w: Source-to-destination delivery. Device: router.

fixed.q: Which is NOT a network-layer function?
fixed.w: Framing, MAC addressing, hop-to-hop flow and error control belong to the data link layer.

fixed.q: Which layer sends data as a raw bit stream?
The data units at the transport, network and data link layers are, respectively:
fixed.w: Messages between transport entities are segments. The TCP/IP internet layer carries packets.

fixed.q: I. OSI layers 1–3 are end-to-end. II. Layers 4–7 are chained. Which is true?
fixed.w: It's the other way round: 1–3 chained (hop-by-hop), 4–7 end-to-end.

fixed.q: The transport layer provides ___ delivery, while the data link layer provides ___ delivery.
fixed.w: Network layer: host-to-host (source-to-destination).

fixed.q: The TCP/IP model has how many layers (standard)?
fixed.w: Application, transport, internet, network access. (A hybrid 5-layer model also exists.)

fixed.q: A repeater operates only in the ___ layer.
fixed.w: Repeater and hub: physical. Bridge and switch: data link. Router: network. Gateway: all layers.

fixed.q: Which device works at the network layer of the OSI model?
Frames from one LAN can be transmitted to another LAN via a:
fixed.w: A bridge filters by MAC address; a switch is a multiport bridge.

fixed.q: A switch differs from a hub because a switch:
o: Forwards a frame only to the destination port using MAC addresses
fixed.w: Hub = multiport repeater, one collision domain. Each switch port = own collision domain; each router port = own broadcast domain.

fixed.q: Which device joins networks that use different protocols (protocol converter)?
Which guided medium is graded by RG (Radio Government) ratings?
fixed.w: RG-59 cable TV, RG-58 thin Ethernet.

fixed.q: Optical fibre carries light by:
o: Total internal reflection, the core being denser than the cladding
fixed.w: Fibre: highest bandwidth, no EM interference, hard to tap; costly to install.

fixed.q: Unguided media: I. Carry EM waves without a physical conductor. II. Signals can travel by ground propagation. Which is correct?
fixed.w: Ground (low freq), sky (ionosphere, 3–30 MHz), line-of-sight propagation.

fixed.q: Which waves are unidirectional, need aligned antennas and cannot penetrate walls?
fixed.w: Radio: omnidirectional, penetrates walls. Infrared: short range (TV remote).

fixed.q: Which formula gives the wavelength of a signal?
fixed.w: Equivalently λ = speed / frequency.

fixed.q: Which is NOT a parameter used to describe a sine wave?
fixed.w: Wavelength is derived from speed and frequency.

fixed.q: Baud rate means:
o: The number of signal changes per second
The number of bits per second
fixed.w: Bit rate = baud × bits per signal element.

fixed.q: Shannon's channel capacity is:
fixed.w: Nyquist (noiseless): bit rate = 2B log₂ L.

fixed.q: A 6 kHz channel with SNR = 16 has a Shannon capacity of about:
fixed.w: 6000 × log₂17 ≈ 6000 × 4.09 ≈ 24.5 kbps. (The paper's closest option, and key, was 24.74 kbps.)

fixed.q: At 100% amplitude modulation, the power in each sideband is what fraction of the carrier power?
fixed.w: Both sidebands together = 50% of carrier.

fixed.q: With Manchester encoding in Ethernet, the pulse width compared with straight binary encoding is:
fixed.w: A transition in the middle of every bit → self-clocking; baud = 2 × bit rate.

fixed.q: The two IEEE sublayers of the data link layer are:
fixed.w: LLC: flow and error control. MAC: access method and addressing.

fixed.q: In the data link layer, ___ is based on automatic repeat request (retransmission).
Bit stuffing refers to:
o: Inserting a 0 into user data after five consecutive 1s so it is not mistaken for the flag
Appending a nibble to the flag
Appending a nibble to the data
fixed.w: HDLC flag 01111110.

fixed.q: Error detection at the data link level is achieved by:
Which statement is NOT true?
o: CRC stands for Code Repeat Check
CRC stands for Cyclic Redundancy Check
A zero remainder at the receiver means no error detected

fixed.q: To guarantee correction of up to 5 errors, the minimum Hamming distance must be:
fixed.w: Correct t errors: d ≥ 2t + 1. Detect s errors: d ≥ s + 1.

fixed.q: For 40 data bits, the Hamming code needs how many bits in total?
fixed.w: Smallest r with 2^r ≥ m + r + 1: r = 6 → 46.

fixed.q: Divisor 1011, dataword 1001. The CRC is:
A simple even-parity bit can detect:
o: Any odd number of bit errors
Any even number of bit errors
fixed.w: d_min = 2. Two-dimensional parity detects up to 3 errors.

fixed.q: Which type of error is more common?
fixed.w: Noise usually affects a group of bits.

fixed.q: In Go-Back-N ARQ with m-bit sequence numbers, the send and receive window sizes are:
fixed.w: Selective Repeat: both 2^(m−1). Stop-and-wait: 1 and 1.

fixed.q: Which ARQ retransmits only the lost or damaged frames and needs a timer per frame?
fixed.w: GBN resends all frames from the lost one, with one timer.

fixed.q: Stop-and-wait efficiency is:
fixed.w: Tt = L/B, Tp = distance/speed. GBN window for full use = 1 + 2a.

fixed.q: Piggybacking means:
o: Sending the ACK inside a data frame going the other way

fixed.q: The maximum throughput of pure ALOHA and slotted ALOHA is:
fixed.w: Pure S = G e^(−2G), max at G = 0.5; slotted S = G e^(−G), max at G = 1. Vulnerable time 2Tfr vs Tfr.

fixed.q: CSMA/CD is used in ___ and CSMA/CA in ___.
fixed.w: Wireless can't detect collisions, so it avoids them (IFS, contention window, ACK; RTS/CTS).

fixed.q: For CSMA/CD to work, the minimum frame transmission time must be at least:
fixed.w: L_min = 2 × Tp × B. Classic Ethernet: 64 bytes (512 bits).

fixed.q: Which CSMA persistence method has the highest chance of collision?
fixed.w: Non-persistent waits a random time when busy: fewer collisions, lower efficiency.

fixed.q: The minimum and maximum Ethernet frame sizes (without preamble) are:
fixed.w: Payload 46–1500 bytes. Preamble 7 B + SFD 1 B, addresses 6 B each, CRC 4 B.

fixed.q: A MAC address is ___ bits long, and the broadcast MAC address is:
fixed.w: Stored on the NIC. Multicast: LSB of first byte = 1.

fixed.q: Which IEEE standard is Wi-Fi?
fixed.w: 802.3 Ethernet, 802.4 token bus, 802.5 token ring, 802.15 Bluetooth, 802.16 WiMAX.

fixed.q: In IPv4, every IP address has how many bits? And IPv6?
A 4-byte IP address consists of:
The first-octet range of class B addresses is:
Which is a private IP address?
The default subnet masks of classes A, B and C are:
fixed.w: The DSSSB 2017 key answered 'All of the above' for 'default subnet mask for a class'.

fixed.q: A network with mask 255.255.240.0 can have at most how many hosts?
fixed.w: 12 host bits: 2¹² − 2 = 4094.

fixed.q: Network 192.168.10.0 needs at least 25 hosts per subnet with the most subnets possible. Which mask?
fixed.w: /27 → 30 hosts per subnet, 8 subnets.

fixed.q: A network needs 29 subnets. How many bits must be borrowed from the host field?
The limited broadcast address is:
o: The network ID with host bits 0
fixed.w: Directed broadcast = network ID with all host bits 1.

fixed.q: If the TTL field is 10, then:
o: At most 10 routers can process the datagram
At most 11 routers can process it
fixed.w: Each router decrements TTL by 1 and discards at 0, sending ICMP time exceeded.

fixed.q: In ICMP time-exceeded handling, each router the datagram visits:
Which IPv4 header field is NOT related to fragmentation?
fixed.w: Offset is in units of 8 bytes; header 20–60 bytes; total length max 65,535.

fixed.q: The IPv4 header checksum covers:
o: Only the header, recalculated at every router
fixed.w: TCP checksum covers the segment + pseudo-header (mandatory); UDP checksum optional in IPv4.

fixed.q: Which protocol converts IP addresses to physical (MAC) addresses?
fixed.w: ARP request is broadcast, reply unicast. RARP: MAC → IP (diskless machines).

fixed.q: ICMP stands for:
fixed.w: ICMP reports errors (destination unreachable, time exceeded…) to the source; ping uses echo request/reply.

fixed.q: Which protocols assign IP addresses dynamically? i) POP ii) DHCP iii) BOOTP iv) SNMP v) ICMP
o: ii, iii, iv and v only
i, ii, iii and v only
fixed.w: DHCP automates IP, mask, gateway and DNS (UDP 67/68).

fixed.q: The algorithm that manages routing tables and makes routing decisions is the:
Distance vector routing uses ___ and suffers from ___.
fixed.w: RIP = distance vector (hop count, infinity = 16). OSPF = link state (Dijkstra). BGP = path vector between ASes.

fixed.q: Link-state routing shares ___ with ___.
o: knowledge of its neighbours; the whole internet
its whole table; the whole internet
fixed.w: Distance vector shares its whole table with neighbours.

fixed.q: Which routing algorithm is used in MANETs?
As per the NIC 2020 key, a router table contains addresses belonging to ___ protocol(s).
Too many packets in part of the network, causing delay and loss, is called:
fixed.w: It occurs because routers and switches have queues that fill.

fixed.q: Why does congestion occur?
o: Because routers and switches have queues

fixed.q: Which traffic-shaping algorithm allows bursts up to the saved tokens?
fixed.w: Leaky bucket outputs at a constant rate.

fixed.q: Which are transport-layer protocols?
Which statement about TCP is FALSE?
o: It treats data as a byte stream

fixed.q: Which protocol lets applications send encapsulated IP datagrams without establishing a connection?
fixed.w: UDP header = 8 bytes; no flow, error (except checksum) or congestion control. Used by DNS, TFTP, SNMP, RIP, VoIP.

fixed.q: Which transport-layer feature prevents data loss when the sender is faster than the receiver?
Because sending and receiving TCP processes may work at different speeds, TCP needs ___ for storage.
During TCP slow start, the congestion window:
fixed.w: Above ssthresh: congestion avoidance (+1 MSS per RTT). Timeout: ssthresh = cwnd/2, cwnd = 1.

fixed.q: The TCP header is ___ and the UDP header is ___.
fixed.w: TCP flags: URG, ACK, PSH, RST, SYN, FIN.

fixed.q: Port numbers are ___ bits; well-known ports are:
fixed.w: Registered 1024–49151; dynamic/ephemeral 49152–65535.

fixed.q: Match old TCP ports: 7, 9, 11, 13 with Daytime, Echo, Discard, SYSTAT.
Which well-known port pairs are correct?
fixed.w: FTP 20/21, SSH 22, TELNET 23, DNS 53, DHCP 67/68, TFTP 69, IMAP 143, SNMP 161.

fixed.q: To retrieve mail via the IMAP daemon, a process connects to port:
Which protocol is used for sending email?
fixed.w: SMTP pushes mail (port 25); POP3 (110) and IMAP4 (143) pull it. MIME carries non-ASCII content.

fixed.q: FTP uses:
o: Two TCP connections: control on port 21 and data on port 20
fixed.w: TFTP: UDP port 69, no authentication. Anonymous FTP: log in as 'anonymous'.

fixed.q: DNS maps:
fixed.w: Hierarchy: root → TLD → authoritative servers. UDP port 53.

fixed.q: HTTP is stateless. What makes web sessions stateful?
fixed.w: HTTP 1.1 uses persistent connections by default.

fixed.q: Which protocol automatically configures IP address, subnet mask, DNS and default gateway?
Socket and Winsock are examples of:
Which old protocol is used for uploading and downloading files between computers (over modems)?
The information transformed during encryption is called:
fixed.w: Plain text in, cipher text out.

fixed.q: The process of verifying a user's identity is:
Which cipher reorders letters without disguising them?
fixed.w: Substitution replaces letters.

fixed.q: Which is NOT a symmetric-key algorithm?
fixed.w: RSA is public-key (asymmetric).

fixed.q: The key length of Triple DES is:
fixed.w: DES 56 bits; 3DES 3 × 56 = 168.

fixed.q: A key used to encrypt one communication session between end systems is a:
A digital signature is required for:
o: Non-repudiation of communication by the sender
fixed.w: The nonrepudiation service protects against repudiation.

fixed.q: Which two protocols does IPsec define?
Which firewall filters application commands such as HTTP GET/POST?
In a MANET, which attack injects false routing information to route packets into a loop?
BTS in mobile networks stands for:
fixed.w: HLR keeps subscriber home data; VLR keeps visitors' data and updates the HLR.

fixed.q: CDMA is an example of which generation of cellular networks (per the key)?
fixed.w: IS-95 CDMA was 2G.

fixed.q: Arrange in ascending order of data speed: GSM, LTE, GPRS, EDGE.
In Mobile IP, the router in the foreign network to which the mobile node is attached is the:
fixed.w: The care-of address (COA) is the current tunnel endpoint, which can be obtained via DHCP.

fixed.q: Handover from a satellite network to a terrestrial cellular network is:
Which factors affect the transmission rate in DSL?
o: Wire gauge of the twisted pair and electrical interference

fixed.q: In optical distribution architecture, which is actually an Ethernet switch?
fixed.w: PON uses passive splitters.

fixed.q: In a global system of world-wide computer networks, interconnection is essential for which purpose of computations?
fixed.w: Interconnection in a worldwide network is essential for exchanging messages for communication.

fixed.q: Which of the following is designed in such a way that all the stations are connected through a single cable known as a backbone cable in the computer network?
fixed.w: In a bus topology all stations connect to a single backbone cable.

fixed.q: Which of the following is FALSE with reference to a peer-to-peer network?
o: This network has a dedicated server.
It is useful for small environments, usually up to 10 computers.
Special permissions are assigned to each computer for sharing the resources.
All the computers are linked together with equal privilege and responsibilities for processing data.
fixed.w: A peer-to-peer network has no dedicated server, so A is false.

fixed.q: Which of the following belongs to the fixed and wireless configuration category of mobile devices?
fixed.w: The Wi-Fi router: it sits in a fixed location yet connects devices wirelessly.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Circuit setup is not required in both a datagram network and virtual-circuit network.
Circuit setup is required in both a datagram network and virtual-circuit network.
Circuit setup is required in a virtual-circuit network.
Circuit setup is required in a datagram network.
fixed.w: Virtual-circuit networks set up a path (circuit) before data transfer; datagram networks don't.

fixed.q: The disadvantage of using parallel mode of communication is
fixed.w: Parallel transmission needs many wires, so it is costly, especially over long distances.

fixed.q: In which of the following radio channel sharing methods several users share the same frequency channel of higher bandwidth by dividing it into different time slots?
fixed.w: TDMA divides one frequency channel into time slots for different users.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is true about Home Location Register (HLR) and Visitor Location Register (VLR)?
o: VLR is responsible for the MS (Mobile Station) to inform the HLR about location changes.
VLR is not responsible for the MS (Mobile Station) to inform the MLR about location changes.
VLR is not responsible for the MS (Mobile Station) to inform the HLR about location changes.
HLR is responsible for the MS (Mobile Station) to inform the VLR about location changes.
fixed.w: When the mobile moves, the new VLR informs the HLR of the location change.

fixed.q: Mobile Agents are also called ______ agents. They are of two types: Mobile Agents with pre-defined path and Mobile Agents with undefined path.
fixed.w: Mobile agents are also called transportable agents.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) Service Set Identification (SSID) is a human-readable text string with a maximum length of 2000 bytes. ii) SSID acts as a single shared identifier between the access points and clients.
fixed.w: An SSID is at most 32 characters (not 2000 bytes), and it is shared by APs and clients. So i false, ii true.

fixed.q: Which of the following are limitations of mobile computing? i) Device mobility ii) Power consumption iii) Human interface with device iv) Range and bandwidth v) Transmission interferences vi) Wireless connectivity
o: ii, iii, iv and v only
fixed.w: Mobile computing is limited by power, the human interface, range and bandwidth, and interference.

fixed.q:
Match the column Mobility with the column Descriptions.
Mobility: a) Macro-mobility; b) Micro-mobility; c) Ad hoc mobility

Descriptions: i) Mobility within a MANET, caused by device mobility constantly changing the network topology; ii) Mobility through a global network; iii) Mobility of a device in one single administrative domain of the global network.
fixed.w: Macro = across the global network (ii), micro = within one administrative domain (iii), ad hoc = within a MANET (i).

fixed.q: Which of the following factors affect(s) the transmission rate in DSL?
o: Both the gauge of the twisted-pair line and the degree of electrical interference
fixed.w: DSL speed depends on loop length, wire gauge and interference. Shadow fading is a wireless effect.

fixed.q: If the channel is band-limited to 6 kHz and the signal-to-noise ratio is 16, what would be the capacity of the channel?
fixed.w: C = B·log2(1 + S/N) = 6000 × log2 17 ≈ 6000 × 4.09 ≈ 24.5 kbps, closest to 24.74 kbps.

fixed.q: In a computer communication network the term baud rate means
o: The number of bits transmitted per unit time
The number of bytes lost per unit time
The rate at which signal changes
fixed.w: Baud rate is the number of signal changes (symbols) per second.

fixed.q: ______ is the address of the current tunnel endpoint for the MN that can be chosen via DHCP.
fixed.w: The care-of address (COA) is the current tunnel endpoint for the mobile node; a co-located COA can be obtained via DHCP. The official key says FA. (The official key was wrong here; this is the corrected answer.)

fixed.q: Default subnet mask for a class
fixed.w: 255.0.0.0, 255.255.0.0 and 255.255.255.0 are the default masks of classes A, B and C respectively.

fixed.q: Which of the following security services protects against repudiation?
fixed.w: The non-repudiation service protects against denial of sending or receiving.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is true about the slow start phase of TCP congestion control?
o: Congestion window approximately doubles every round trip time.
Congestion window increases by 1 Maximum Segment Size every round trip time.
Congestion window increases by 2 Maximum Segment Size on every successful acknowledgement.
Congestion window approximately doubles on every successful acknowledgement.
fixed.w: In slow start, cwnd grows by 1 MSS per ACK, so it roughly doubles every RTT.

fixed.q:
Match the well-known ports used by TCP with the protocols.
Ports: a) 7; b) 9; c) 11; d) 13

Protocols: i) Daytime; ii) Echo; iii) Discard; iv) SYSTAT
fixed.w: Ports: 7 = Echo, 9 = Discard, 11 = SYSTAT, 13 = Daytime.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) In connectionless services of a transport layer protocol, the packets are sent from one party to another with no need for connection establishment or connection release. ii) In connection-oriented service of a transport layer protocol, a connection is first established between the sender and the receiver. iii) The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is called a connectionless, unreliable transport protocol.
fixed.w: All three statements about connectionless and connection-oriented service and UDP are true.

fixed.q: The internet layer in the TCP/IP model is associated with ______ data.
fixed.w: The internet (network) layer handles packets (datagrams).

fixed.q: Which of the following refers to messages sent from transport entity to transport entity in the transport layer of the ISO/OSI network model?
fixed.w: Segment: transport-layer messages are called segments (TPDUs).

fixed.q: Delimiting and synchronisation of data exchange is provided by which layer?
fixed.w: The session layer manages dialogue and inserts synchronisation points (checkpoints) in the data exchange.

fixed.q: If the original size of data is 40, then after adding error-detection redundancy bits the size of the data is
fixed.w: Hamming code needs r bits with 2^r ≥ m + r + 1. For m = 40, r = 6, giving 46 bits.

fixed.q: Bit stuffing refers to
o: Inserting a '0' in the user data stream to differentiate it from a flag
Inserting a '0' in the flag stream to avoid ambiguity
Appending a nibble to the flag sequence
Appending a nibble to the user data stream
fixed.w: In HDLC, after five consecutive 1s in the data a 0 is stuffed, so the data never looks like the flag 01111110.

fixed.q: Any process in the transport layer wishing to remotely retrieve mail from a host can connect to the destination host's port ______ to contact its IMAP daemon.
fixed.w: IMAP listens on TCP port 143 (993 with TLS).

fixed.q: Which of the following does anonymous FTP refer to?
o: A protocol that requires a password
fixed.w: Anonymous FTP lets anyone download public files over the Internet's file transfer protocol using the login "anonymous", with no personal password.

fixed.q: GSM is a mobile technology of which generation?
fixed.w: 1G analogue (AMPS), 2G digital GSM/CDMA, 2.5G GPRS, 2.75G EDGE, 3G UMTS/WCDMA, 4G LTE, 5G NR.

fixed.q: GSM uses which combination of access methods?
fixed.w: GSM divides the band into carriers (FDMA) and each carrier into 8 time slots (TDMA).

fixed.q: GPRS added which capability to GSM networks?
fixed.w: GPRS (2.5G) brought packet-switched data over GSM, billed by data rather than by time.

fixed.q: 4G LTE uses which multiple-access technique in the downlink?
fixed.w: LTE uses OFDMA downlink and SC-FDMA uplink, with an all-IP core.

fixed.q: In cellular networks, cells are usually modelled as which shape?
fixed.w: Hexagons cover an area with no gaps or overlaps and approximate circular coverage.

fixed.q: Using the same frequencies in cells that are far enough apart is called:
fixed.w: Frequency reuse increases capacity; co-channel cells are separated to limit interference.

fixed.q: Transferring an ongoing call from one cell to another as the user moves is:
fixed.w: Handoff keeps the call alive when the mobile crosses cell boundaries. Hard handoff breaks before making; soft handoff (CDMA) makes before breaking.

fixed.q: In GSM, the database that stores permanent subscriber information is the:
fixed.w: HLR: permanent subscriber data. VLR: temporary data for visitors in an MSC area. EIR: equipment identity. AuC: authentication.

fixed.q: In Mobile IP, the address a mobile node uses while in a foreign network is the:
fixed.w: The home agent tunnels packets to the care-of address registered through the foreign agent.

fixed.q: A Bluetooth piconet can have one master and at most how many active slaves?
fixed.w: A piconet has 1 master + up to 7 active slaves (8 devices). Linked piconets form a scatternet.

fixed.q: Bluetooth operates in which frequency band?
fixed.w: Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz ISM band with frequency hopping.

fixed.q: The IEEE standard for Bluetooth (WPAN) is:
fixed.w: 802.11 Wi-Fi (WLAN), 802.15.1 Bluetooth, 802.15.4 Zigbee, 802.16 WiMAX, 802.3 Ethernet.

fixed.q: A network of mobile nodes with no fixed infrastructure is a:
fixed.w: In a MANET each node also acts as a router. AODV and DSR are on-demand routing protocols for MANETs.

fixed.q: WAP pages for early mobile phones were written in:
fixed.w: WAP (Wireless Application Protocol) used WML (Wireless Markup Language) shown as cards in a deck.

fixed.q: The hidden terminal problem in wireless LANs is reduced using:
fixed.w: 802.11 uses CSMA/CA with optional RTS/CTS so hidden stations learn the medium is busy.

fixed.q: Which mobile OS is based on the Linux kernel?
fixed.w: Android (Google) uses a modified Linux kernel. iOS is based on Darwin (XNU).

fixed.q: A SIM card in a GSM phone mainly stores:
fixed.w: The SIM holds the IMSI and authentication key Ki. The IMEI identifies the handset itself.

fixed.q: The number of bits transmitted per second is called:
fixed.w: Bit rate = bits/s; baud rate = signal elements/s. Bit rate = baud rate × bits per signal element.

fixed.q: A signal carries 4 bits per signal element at 1000 baud. Its bit rate is:
fixed.w: Bit rate = baud × bits per element = 1000 × 4.

fixed.q: The range of frequencies a channel can pass is its:
fixed.w: Bandwidth (Hz) = highest − lowest frequency passed.

fixed.q: Frequency and period of a signal are related as:
fixed.w: Frequency is the reciprocal of the period.

fixed.q: Nyquist bit rate for a noiseless channel of bandwidth B with L signal levels is:
fixed.w: Nyquist: 2B log₂L. Shannon (noisy channel): B log₂(1+SNR).

fixed.q: The maximum data rate of a NOISY channel is given by:
fixed.w: C = B log₂(1 + SNR).

fixed.q: The position of a waveform relative to time zero is its:
fixed.w: Peak amplitude, frequency and phase are the three parameters of a sine wave.

fixed.q: Which line coding has a transition in the MIDDLE of every bit, giving self-synchronisation?
fixed.w: Manchester (used in classic Ethernet) has a mid-bit transition, so each pulse is half a bit wide.

fixed.q: Converting digital data into an analog signal for transmission over telephone lines is done by a:
fixed.w: Modulator–demodulator. A codec does the reverse (analog → digital).

fixed.q: Varying the amplitude of a carrier to represent data is:
fixed.w: ASK changes amplitude; FSK changes frequency; PSK changes phase.

fixed.q: Transmission in which data flows in both directions but only one direction at a time is:
fixed.w: Walkie-talkie = half duplex; telephone = full duplex; keyboard/TV = simplex.

fixed.q: The block size of DES is:
fixed.w: DES: 64-bit block, 56-bit effective key, 16 rounds.

fixed.q: The key length options of AES are:
fixed.w: AES block = 128 bits; keys 128/192/256.

fixed.q: A digital signature is created by encrypting the message hash with the:
fixed.w: Anyone can verify it with the sender's public key, giving authentication and non-repudiation.

fixed.q: Which security service ensures that data has NOT been altered in transit?
fixed.w: Integrity → hashes/MACs; confidentiality → encryption.

fixed.q: MD5 and SHA-256 are examples of:
fixed.w: A hash maps any input to a fixed-length digest (MD5 128-bit, SHA-256 256-bit).

fixed.q: A firewall that filters packets only on IP address, port and protocol is a:
fixed.w: Packet filters work at network/transport layers; application gateways inspect application commands.

fixed.q: Flooding a server with traffic from many compromised machines so it cannot serve users is a:
fixed.w: Distributed Denial of Service attacks availability.

fixed.q: SSL/TLS mainly provides security at which level?
fixed.w: HTTPS = HTTP over TLS. IPsec works at the network layer.

fixed.q: Hiding a secret message inside an image or audio file is:
fixed.w: Cryptography hides meaning; steganography hides existence.

fixed.q: GSM is a ___ generation cellular technology.
fixed.w: 1G analog (AMPS), 2G GSM/CDMA, 3G UMTS/WCDMA, 4G LTE, 5G NR.

fixed.q: LTE is associated with which generation?
fixed.w: Long Term Evolution = 4G.

fixed.q: The IEEE standard for Wi-Fi (wireless LAN) is:
fixed.w: 802.3 Ethernet, 802.11 Wi-Fi, 802.15 Bluetooth/PAN, 802.16 WiMAX.

fixed.q: Bluetooth is an example of a:
fixed.w: Personal Area Network, about 10 m.

fixed.q: A wireless network with no fixed infrastructure where nodes act as routers is a:
fixed.w: Mobile Ad hoc NETwork; AODV and DSR are its routing protocols.

fixed.q: In cellular networks, dividing an area into cells so the same frequencies can be used in distant cells is:
fixed.w: Frequency reuse raises capacity.

fixed.q: The physical address burned into a NIC is the:
fixed.w: MAC addresses are 48-bit, written as 6 hex pairs.

fixed.q: A network in which every computer can act as both client and server is:
fixed.w: P2P has no dedicated server.

fixed.q: A network spanning a city, such as a cable-TV network, is a:
fixed.w: PAN < LAN < MAN < WAN by area.

fixed.q: In which topology does failure of the central device bring the whole network down?
fixed.w: All nodes in a star connect through one hub/switch.

fixed.q: Number of links needed for a full mesh of n devices:
fixed.w: Each pair needs a dedicated link.

fixed.q: Which topology uses a single backbone cable with terminators at both ends?
fixed.w: A break in the backbone disables a bus network.

fixed.q: Which range is a private Class A block?
An IPv4 address is ___ bits and an IPv6 address is ___ bits.
fixed.w: IPv6 is written as 8 groups of 4 hex digits.

fixed.q: First octet 192–223 indicates which class?
Default subnet mask of a Class B network:
Number of usable host addresses in a /24 network:
fixed.w: 2⁸ − 2 (network and broadcast addresses excluded).

fixed.q: Default port of HTTP and HTTPS respectively:
fixed.w: Know: FTP 20/21, SSH 22, Telnet 23, SMTP 25, DNS 53, HTTP 80, POP3 110, IMAP 143, HTTPS 443.

fixed.q: DNS normally uses port:
fixed.w: DNS: UDP/TCP 53. SNMP uses 161.

fixed.q: Which protocol is used to SEND email from a client to a mail server?
fixed.w: SMTP sends; POP3 and IMAP retrieve.

fixed.q: Unlike POP3, IMAP lets the user:
o: Keep and organise mail on the server across devices
fixed.w: IMAP (port 143) syncs folders on the server.

fixed.q: Translating a domain name such as www.dsssb.delhi.gov.in into an IP address is done by:
fixed.w: ARP maps IP → MAC; DHCP assigns IP addresses.

fixed.q: Which protocol finds the MAC address for a known IP address?
fixed.w: RARP does the reverse (MAC → IP).

fixed.q: The ping command uses which protocol?
fixed.w: ICMP echo request/echo reply.

fixed.q: Which protocol is used to manage and monitor network devices?
fixed.w: Simple Network Management Protocol (ports 161/162).

fixed.q: A switch operates at which OSI layer?
fixed.w: Hub/repeater L1, switch/bridge L2, router L3, gateway up to L7.

fixed.q: A device connecting networks that use completely different protocols is a:
fixed.w: Gateways translate between protocol stacks.

fixed.q: Which transport protocol is connectionless and has no acknowledgements?
fixed.w: UDP is used for DNS queries, streaming, VoIP.

fixed.q: TCP connection establishment uses a:
fixed.w: Connection release uses a four-way FIN/ACK exchange.

fixed.q: In which switching technique is a dedicated path reserved for the whole call?
fixed.w: Telephone networks are circuit-switched; the internet is packet-switched.

fixed.q: Dividing a link by giving each user a different frequency band is:
fixed.w: FDM by frequency, TDM by time slot, WDM by light wavelength (optical fibre).

fixed.q: Which transmission medium is immune to electromagnetic interference?
fixed.w: Fibre carries light by total internal reflection.

fixed.q: Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) is used in:
fixed.w: WDM is conceptually FDM applied to different wavelengths of light.

fixed.q: FM radio stations sharing the air by each using a different carrier frequency is an example of:
fixed.w: Each station gets its own frequency band, so it is frequency division multiplexing.

fixed.q: In synchronous TDM, bandwidth is wasted when:
o: A source has no data to send in its fixed slot
fixed.w: Statistical (asynchronous) TDM gives slots only to sources that have data.

fixed.q: Statistical TDM differs from synchronous TDM because it:
o: Allocates slots dynamically to sources that have data
Gives every source a fixed slot
fixed.w: Each slot must therefore carry an address identifying the source.

fixed.q: In CDMA, users share the channel by:
o: Transmitting at the same time on the same band, each with a unique code
fixed.w: The receiver separates a user's signal using that user's code.

fixed.q: A multiplexer that combines n input lines onto one link needs, at the receiving end, a:
fixed.w: The DEMUX separates the signal back into its n channels.

fixed.q: The IEEE standard for Ethernet is:
fixed.w: 802.11 is Wi-Fi, 802.5 Token Ring and 802.15 Bluetooth.

fixed.q: Classic (shared-medium) Ethernet uses the access method:
fixed.w: Collision detection. Wi-Fi uses CSMA/CA (collision avoidance).

fixed.q: In 10BASE-T, 'BASE' and 'T' stand for:
fixed.w: 10 Mbps, baseband signalling, twisted-pair cable.

fixed.q: Fast Ethernet operates at:
fixed.w: Gigabit Ethernet = 1000 Mbps (1000BASE-T).

fixed.q: The error-detection field in an Ethernet frame is the:
fixed.w: The frame check sequence is 4 bytes at the end of the frame.

fixed.q: The line encoding used by 10 Mbps Ethernet is:
fixed.w: Manchester has a transition in the middle of every bit, which gives clock synchronisation.

theory.Basics:
• Data communication: message, sender, receiver, medium, protocol (syntax, semantics, timing). A protocol fixes format/rules, not the message content.
• Point-to-point = dedicated link; multipoint = shared link.
• Modes: simplex (keyboard, radio), half duplex (walkie-talkie), full duplex (telephone). No 'half simplex'.
• Peer-to-peer: all equal, no dedicated server (≈10 PCs). Client/server: server + clients. Proxy server filters web traffic.
• Parallel transmission is costly (many wires); serial is cheaper.
• Essentials for Internet: NIC + TCP/IP.
theory.Topology:
• Mesh: n(n−1)/2 links, n−1 ports each; robust, costly.
• Star: central hub; hub failure kills all; adding nodes doesn't slow it.
• Bus: one backbone cable with taps; a break stops all.
• Ring: each node has 2 neighbours and a repeater; all equal, no host; a break can stop it.
• Hybrid/tree combine these.
theory.Network types: • PAN (~10 m, Bluetooth) < LAN (building; fastest, fewest errors, private) < MAN (city; collection of LANs; data + voice) < WAN (country; satellites/microwave; slowest).
theory.Switching:
• Circuit switching: dedicated path set up first (telephone); no headers, constant delay, wastes idle capacity.
• Packet switching: no reservation. Datagram (independent packets, out of order possible; Internet/IP) vs virtual circuit (path set first; X.25, Frame Relay, ATM).
• Message switching: store-and-forward whole messages.
theory.Multiplexing:
• Multiplexer combines many low-speed lines into one high-speed line. TDM = time slots; FDM = frequency bands (WDM for light).
• Channel access: TDMA (time slots), FDMA (bands), CDMA (codes).
theory.OSI model:
• 7 layers (top → bottom): Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical — 'All People Seem To Need Data Processing'.
• Presentation: translation, encryption, compression. Session: dialog control, token management, synchronisation/checkpoints. Transport: process-to-process, ports, segmentation, end-to-end flow/error control. Network: host-to-host, logical (IP) addressing, routing, congestion. Data link: hop-to-hop, framing, MAC addressing, flow & error control (ARQ). Physical: bits, encoding, data rate.
• Data units: message → segment → packet/datagram → frame → bits.
• Layers 1–3 chained (hop-by-hop); 4–7 end-to-end.
• TCP/IP: application, transport, internet, network access (4 layers).
theory.Devices:
• Physical layer: repeater (regenerates signal), hub (multiport repeater; one collision domain).
• Data link: bridge (joins two LANs by MAC), switch (multiport bridge; sends only to destination port).
• Network: router (IP, routing table; separates broadcast domains).
• Gateway: protocol converter, can work at all layers. Modem: digital ↔ analogue. NIC holds the 48-bit MAC.
theory.Media:
• Guided: twisted pair (UTP/STP, RJ-45), coaxial (RG ratings: RG-59 cable TV, RG-58 thin Ethernet), fibre optic (light by total internal reflection; core denser than cladding; highest bandwidth, immune to EM noise).
• Unguided: ground (low freq), sky (ionosphere, 3–30 MHz), line-of-sight.
• Radio 3 kHz–1 GHz omnidirectional, penetrates walls; microwave 1–300 GHz unidirectional, aligned antennas, no walls; infrared short range (TV remote).
theory.Signals:
• Sine wave: peak amplitude, frequency, phase. λ = speed × period = speed / frequency.
• Baud rate = signal changes per second; bit rate = baud × bits per signal element.
• Nyquist (noiseless): bit rate = 2B log₂ L. Shannon: C = B log₂(1 + SNR) (SNR linear).
• Manchester: mid-bit transition, self-clocking, pulse width half of NRZ (baud = 2 × bit rate); used by 10 Mbps Ethernet.
• AM at 100% modulation: each sideband = 25% of carrier power.
theory.Data link:
• Sublayers: LLC (flow/error control) and MAC (access, addressing).
• Tt = L/B; Tp = distance/speed; a = Tp/Tt.
• Stop-and-wait: windows 1/1; η = 1/(1 + 2a).
• Go-Back-N: send window 2^m − 1, receive 1, one timer, resend all from the lost frame, cumulative ACK. Window for full use = 1 + 2a.
• Selective Repeat: both windows 2^(m−1), timer per frame, NAK, resend only lost frames.
• Error control in DLL uses ARQ. Bit stuffing inserts 0 after five 1s (flag 01111110). Piggybacking puts ACKs in data frames.
theory.Error control:
• Burst errors are more common than single-bit errors.
• Hamming distance = number of 1s in x XOR y. Detect s errors: d ≥ s + 1; correct t: d ≥ 2t + 1.
• Parity: detects odd numbers of errors (d = 2). 2-D parity detects up to 3.
• Hamming code: parity bits at 1, 2, 4, 8…; 2^r ≥ m + r + 1 (40 data bits → 6 → 46). C(7,4) has d = 3.
• CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check): append degree-many zeros, divide by generator with XOR, append remainder; receiver remainder 0 = no error. Used at the data link layer.
• Checksum: one's-complement sum, complemented (IP, TCP, UDP).
theory.MAC:
• Pure ALOHA: S = G e^(−2G), max 18.4% at G = 0.5, vulnerable 2Tfr. Slotted: S = G e^(−G), max 36.8% at G = 1, vulnerable Tfr.
• CSMA: listen before talk; 1-persistent most collisions, non-persistent fewer but less efficient, p-persistent for slotted channels.
• CSMA/CD (wired Ethernet 802.3): Tfr ≥ 2Tp → L_min = 2·Tp·B (64 bytes at 10 Mbps). CSMA/CA (Wi-Fi 802.11): IFS, contention window, ACK, RTS/CTS.
• Controlled access: reservation, polling, token passing.
theory.Ethernet:
• IEEE 802.3, CSMA/CD, Manchester (10 Mbps), connectionless, unreliable.
• Frame: preamble 7 B + SFD 1 B, dest 6, src 6, type 2, data 46–1500, CRC 4. Frame 64–1518 bytes.
• MAC 48 bits; broadcast FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF.
• 802.3 Ethernet, 802.4 token bus, 802.5 token ring (IBM), 802.11 Wi-Fi, 802.15 Bluetooth, 802.16 WiMAX. FDDI: dual fibre ring, 100 Mbps.
theory.IP addressing:
• IPv4 32 bits (dotted decimal); IPv6 128 bits. Address = network ID + host ID.
• Classes by first octet: A 0–127 (mask 255.0.0.0), B 128–191 (255.255.0.0), C 192–223 (255.255.255.0), D 224–239 multicast, E 240–255 reserved. 127.x = loopback.
• Hosts per network = 2^h − 2 (network and broadcast addresses).
• Private: 10/8, 172.16–172.31, 192.168/16 (via NAT). Limited broadcast 255.255.255.255; directed = host bits all 1.
• Subnetting borrows host bits: n subnets → ⌈log₂ n⌉ bits. CIDR a.b.c.d/n: block = 2^(32−n); first = AND mask; last = host bits all 1. Supernetting combines blocks (fewer 1s in mask).
theory.IP header:
• IPv4: unreliable, connectionless, best-effort. Header 20–60 bytes (HLEN in 4-byte words); total length ≤ 65,535.
• Fragmentation fields: identification, flags (DF, MF), offset (8-byte units). TOS is not about fragmentation. Reassembly only at the destination; MTU (Ethernet) 1500.
• TTL decremented by 1 per router; at 0 discarded + ICMP time exceeded (TTL 10 → at most 10 routers).
• Protocol field: TCP 6, UDP 17, ICMP 1. Header checksum covers only the header, recomputed at each router.
theory.Network protocols:
• ARP: IP → MAC (request broadcast, reply unicast). RARP: MAC → IP (diskless). BOOTP/DHCP assign IP automatically.
• ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol): reports errors to the source — destination unreachable, source quench, time exceeded, parameter problem, redirect; echo request/reply = ping.
• IGMP: multicast group management.
theory.Routing:
• Distance vector: share whole table with neighbours; Bellman-Ford; count-to-infinity (fix: split horizon, poison reverse); RIP (hop count, ∞ = 16).
• Link state: share neighbour info with everyone (flooding LSPs); Dijkstra; OSPF.
• Inside an AS: RIP, OSPF. Between ASes: BGP (path vector).
• MANET: AODV. Flooding needs no table but creates duplicates.
• A routing table holds addresses of a single protocol.
theory.Congestion:
• Congestion = too many packets; caused by router queues filling.
• Open loop: retransmission, window (SR better than GBN), ACK, discard, admission policies. Closed loop: backpressure, choke packet, implicit/explicit signalling.
• Leaky bucket: constant output rate. Token bucket: allows bursts.
theory.Transport:
• Process-to-process delivery; ports 16 bits: well-known 0–1023, registered 1024–49151, dynamic 49152–65535. Socket = IP + port.
• TCP: connection-oriented, reliable, byte stream, full duplex, flow/error/congestion control, 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK), header 20–60 B; flags URG ACK PSH RST SYN FIN. Uses buffers because sender and receiver speeds differ.
• Congestion control: slow start doubles cwnd each RTT up to ssthresh, then +1 MSS/RTT; timeout → cwnd = 1, ssthresh halves.
• UDP: connectionless, unreliable, 8-byte header, optional checksum (IPv4); DNS, TFTP, SNMP, RIP, VoIP. SCTP also transport.
• Old ports: 7 echo, 9 discard, 11 systat, 13 daytime.
theory.Ports: • FTP 20 (data) / 21 (control), SSH 22, TELNET 23, SMTP 25, DNS 53, DHCP 67/68, TFTP 69, HTTP 80, POP3 110, IMAP 143, SNMP 161/162, HTTPS 443, RIP 520.
theory.Application:
• E-mail: SMTP (push, 25) sends; POP3 (110) / IMAP4 (143, folders on server, search) retrieve; MIME for non-ASCII.
• FTP: two TCP connections (21 control for the session, 20 data per file); plaintext passwords; anonymous FTP; TFTP over UDP 69. XMODEM: old modem file transfer.
• HTTP: TCP 80, stateless (cookies add state), HTTP/1.1 persistent by default; HTTPS 443.
• DNS: names → IPs; root → TLD → authoritative; UDP 53.
• DHCP automates IP, mask, gateway, DNS. Socket/Winsock = APIs. TELNET remote login (23), replaced by SSH.
theory.Security:
• Plain text → cipher text. Authentication = verifying identity; non-repudiation via digital signatures.
• Symmetric: DES (56-bit), 3DES (168-bit), AES, RC4. Asymmetric: RSA. Session key = per-session symmetric key.
• Transposition cipher reorders letters; substitution replaces them.
• IPsec: AH and ESP. Firewalls: packet filter, circuit-level, application gateway (filters HTTP GET/POST), stateful.
• MANET attacks: Byzantine (false routes into loops), wormhole.
theory.Wireless:
• BTS = Base Transceiver Station; HLR (home), VLR (visitor) location registers.
• Generations: GSM (2G) < GPRS (2.5G) < EDGE (2.75G) < LTE (4G); CDMA keyed as 2G.
• Mobile IP: home agent, foreign agent (router in foreign network), care-of address (tunnel endpoint, may come from DHCP).
• Inter-system handover: satellite ↔ terrestrial. DSL rate depends on wire gauge and interference. AON uses Ethernet switches; PON is passive.
theory.Mobile computing:
• Generations: 1G analogue (AMPS), 2G GSM/CDMA (digital voice, SMS), 2.5G GPRS (packet data), 2.75G EDGE, 3G UMTS/WCDMA, 4G LTE (OFDMA, all-IP), 5G NR (mmWave, low latency).
• GSM: FDMA + TDMA (8 slots), SIM (IMSI, Ki), HLR (permanent), VLR (visitors), MSC, BSC, BTS, EIR, AuC.
• Cellular: hexagonal cells, frequency reuse, handoff (hard/soft), roaming.
• Mobile IP: home agent, foreign agent, care-of address, tunnelling.
• Bluetooth: IEEE 802.15.1, 2.4 GHz, piconet = 1 master + 7 active slaves; scatternet. Wi-Fi 802.11 (CSMA/CA, RTS/CTS for hidden terminal); WiMAX 802.16; Zigbee 802.15.4.
• MANET: infrastructure-less; AODV, DSR on-demand routing. WAP/WML for early phones. Android uses the Linux kernel.
